end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified nearby spinach as having fewer food miles than apples from Shimla or distant mangoes.
Explained that longer journeys use more fuel and may need refrigerated transport and special packaging.
Compared delivery options and chose the 10 km source as using less fuel.
Teach-back was not passed; explanation of pollution and freshness remained incomplete.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, comparing distances, and linking longer journeys with fuel use, refrigerated transport, electricity, and packaging. They used nearby spinach and apples from Shimla to explain the comparison and selected the 10 km option as using less fuel. At home, ask them to compare two foods and name one effect on fuel, pollution, or freshness.
